text: Comparing this period against the same period a year ago is one of the most common reporting asks there is. Here's the function built for it.
A date column, a number of intervals, and a unit — year, quarter, month, week, or day, written unquoted. Positive moves forward in time. Negative moves back.

Whatever month is currently in context, this shifts every one of those dates back a full year, and CALCULATE sums sales over that shifted set. Compare it against plain Total Sales, broken out by month, and you get a clean year-over-year comparison.

Why not just subtract 365 days? Leap years, and months of different lengths, would throw that off. DATEADD works in real calendar terms — a year back always lands on the same month and day; a month back correctly handles February versus March.
